translations.en: From him, from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ:

translations.en: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn wrote to al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام: “May a man perform the salat (prayer) while wearing an izār wrapped around himself over the qamīṣ?” So he wrote: “Yes.”

chunks.arabic_text: كَتَبَ الْحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ إِلَى الْعَبْدِ الصَّالِحِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: هَلْ يُصَلِّي الرَّجُلُ الصَّلَاةَ وَعَلَيْهِ إِزَارٌ مُتَوَشِّحٌ بِهِ فَوْقَ الْقَمِيصِ؟ فَكَتَبَ: نَعَمْ.

translations.en: Thus, the import of these reports is the lifting of prohibition and permissibility, while the earlier reports pertain to virtue and recommendation; and there is no contradiction between them.

chunks.arabic_text: فَالْوَجْهُ فِي هَذِهِ الْأَخْبَارِ رَفْعُ الْحَظْرِ وَالْجَوَازُ، وَالْأَخْبَارُ الْأُولَى مُتَنَاوِلَةٌ لِلْفَضْلِ وَالِاسْتِحْبَابِ، وَلَيْسَ بَيْنَهُمَا تَنَافٍ.

en.summary: This hadith indicates that performing salat (prayer) while wearing an izār wrapped over the qamīṣ is permissible. The concluding statement reconciles the reports by explaining that some narrations indicate mere permissibility, while earlier ones refer to what is more virtuous and recommended.
en.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray while wearing an izār wrapped over the qamīṣ?

key_terms.الْعَبْدِ الصَّالِحِ: a title for the Imam عليه السلام addressed in the report
key_terms.مُتَوَشِّحٌ: wrapped around oneself in a draped manner
key_terms.الْقَمِيصِ: the shirt or tunic worn beneath
